I have done wheat-maize on this land for many years, so I will still follow the same road this year and only adjust a little. I have 8 mu, not very big, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still do not dare cut too much, because if yield drops, that hurts more than wasting a bit of fertilizer. Around here in Quzhou, if wheat wants a steady head and maize wants a full ear, I have to feed the land enough and use my well water at the key times. For wheat, I will put more fertilizer because it stays longer in the field and I count on it for a solid harvest. For maize, I will still use hybrid seed because that gives better ears than old seed if water keeps up. I watch what people around me do, and most families like mine do one main basal application and then chase nitrogen later, with a few sprays when disease, worm, or aphid pressure shows up. I will keep wheat on rotary tillage after maize, and maize I will put in with no-tillage after wheat if I can, because the time is tight and it saves labor for my 2-person household.

decision.reasoning_summary: I will keep the same wheat-maize rotation on all 8 mu, because this is what I know well and it fits our labor and well irrigation. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, give wheat a bit more fertilizer than maize, and make sure water goes on at the important stages instead of saving too hard on irrigation. I do not like taking risks with yield, so my fertilizer rates stay a little on the safe side, close to what has worked before in my own field and in nearby fields.
